elementalRegister.value: Earth (Pentacles; the garden, the coins, the bird)
elementalRegister.note: The Nine of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of self-sufficiency. The garden and the bird mark it as the card of earned independence and enjoyment.

numericalDegree.note: Nine is the number of completion and the threshold of a new cycle. The card is the moment at which the practice of the Eight becomes the enjoyment of the Nine.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Nine is the near-completion of the suit's energy, in its self-sufficient form.

figureType.value: A standing human figure in a garden, with a bird on her gloved hand
figureType.note: The figure is human and at ease. Her standing in the garden marks the card as one of earned enjoyment.

posture.value: Standing upright in the garden, one hand raised with the bird
posture.note: The posture is one of ease: the figure is standing, not working, marking the card as one of the enjoyed abundance.

gesture.value: One hand raised with the bird, the other at the side
gesture.note: The gesture is one of ease and control. The bird is held on the gloved hand, marking the card as one of the trained instinct.

gaze.value: Looking at the bird or at the garden
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the enjoyment. The figure is looking at what she has, not at what she lacks.

movementDirection.note: There is no movement. The card is the still point of the enjoyment.

centralObject.value: The bird and the coins among the vines
centralObject.note: The bird is the trained instinct; the coins are the abundance. Together they mark the card as one of earned enjoyment.

heldObject.value: The bird on the gloved hand
heldObject.note: The bird is held on the glove. The holding is the holding of the trained instinct.

creature.value: A bird (a falcon or hawk) on the gloved hand, and a snail at the feet
creature.note: The bird is the trained instinct; the snail is the small creature of the ground. The two together mark the card as one of the mastered and the small.

tool.note: The tool is the glove, the mark of the trained instinct. It is the instrument of the mastered.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The enjoyment is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: A garden with vines and coins
landscape.note: The landscape is the garden, the place of the abundance. The vines are heavy with coins, marking the growth as fully ripe.

architecture.note: There is no architecture in the foreground, but a distant house. The card is the garden of the earned abundance, with the household as its horizon.

threshold.note: There is no threshold. The card is the enjoyment, not the crossing.

celestialBody.note: There is no celestial body. The enjoyment is ordinary, not cosmic.

weather.note: The weather is fair. The card is the warm day of the enjoyment.

symmetry.value: Balanced (the figure in the centre, the garden around)
symmetry.note: The composition is balanced. The card is the balance of the earned abundance.

repetitionCount.note: The number nine is the number of completion. The nine coins mark the card as one of the fully ripe abundance.

verticalAxis.value: The bird above, the snail below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the bird to the snail. The bird is the trained instinct, the snail is the small creature of the ground.

horizontalAxis.value: The figure in the garden, the coins among the vines
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the garden: the figure stands, the coins are among the vines.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figure is upright and at ease.

clothing.value: A rich robe, a glove on one hand
clothing.note: The rich robe marks the figure as one of the wealth; the glove marks the trained instinct. The card is the enjoyment of the earned abundance.

nudity.note: The figure is clothed. Her enjoyment is mediated by her ordinary dress.

crown.note: There is no crown. The figure is not a ruler; she is the one who has earned.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of enjoyment, not of suffering.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figure is free.

water.note: There is no water. The card is a card of earth, not of water.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of earth, not of fire.

vegetation.note: The vegetation is the vines and the garden. It marks the card as one of the fully ripe abundance.

stone.note: There is no stone in the foreground. The card is a card of the garden, not of the castle.

polarity.note: The Nine of Pentacles' remedy-pair is the Nine of Swords: earth and air, enjoyment and anxiety. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Nine of Pentacles' enjoyment is the Nine of Swords' anxiety: sometimes the enjoyment needs to be corrected by the recognition of what is still feared.

prescribedAct.value: Enjoy one thing today that you have earned, and let the enjoyment be the point.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of enjoyment. The Nine of Pentacles' lesson is that the wealth is not the accumulation; it is the capacity to enjoy.

detailedReading: The Nine of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of self-sufficiency. Its numerical degree is nine — the number of completion and the threshold of a new cycle — and the figure is a standing woman in a garden, with a bird on her gloved hand, and nine coins among the vines. The landscape is the garden, the place of the abundance. There is no written word, no wound, and no binding: the card is a card of human enjoyment, not of suffering, and not of restraint. The symmetry of the composition confirms that it is the balance of the earned abundance. The prescribed act follows from this: enjoy one thing today that you have earned, and let the enjoyment be the point. The remedy is anxiety — the Nine of Swords — because the enjoyment needs to be corrected by the recognition of what is still feared.

name: Ten of Pentacles
symbols: An old figure seated, with a family around — the lineage, gathered.
Ten coins arranged in the Tree of Life pattern — wealth, structured.
An arch — the passage between the generations.
Dogs at the old man's feet — loyalty, kept close.

reading.upright: The Ten of Pentacles is legacy: the wealth that outlives the one who built it, the family that carries it forward.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the legacy is broken: financial loss, a family divided, or the short-term that cannot become a future.

elementalRegister.value: Earth (Pentacles; the coins, the arch, the family)
elementalRegister.note: The Ten of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of legacy. The coins and the arch mark it as the card of the wealth that outlives the one who built it.

numericalDegree.note: Ten is the number of completion and the return to the beginning. The card is the moment at which the enjoyment of the Nine becomes the legacy of the Ten.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Ten is the completion of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: An old human man seated, with a family group around him
figureType.note: The old man is the figure of the legacy; the family is the mark of the lineage. The two together mark the card as one of the continuity.

posture.value: Seated, the family standing or gathered
posture.note: The posture is one of gathering: the old man is seated, the family is around, marking the card as one of the assembled lineage.

gesture.value: The old man with the dogs at his feet, the family around
gesture.note: The gesture is one of ease and inclusion. The dogs at the feet mark the loyalty, the family around marks the continuity.

gaze.value: The old man looking at the family or the coins; the family around
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the legacy. The old man looks at the family and the coins, marking the card as one of the past looking at the future.

movementDirection.note: There is no movement. The card is the still point of the lineage.

centralObject.value: The ten coins in the Tree of Life pattern and the arch
centralObject.note: The coins are the wealth, structured. The arch is the passage between the generations. Together they mark the card as one of the legacy.

heldObject.value: Absent (the coins are arranged, not held)
heldObject.note: The coins are arranged, not held. The card is the structure of the wealth, not the holding of it.

creature.value: Dogs at the old man's feet
creature.note: The dogs are the creatures of loyalty, kept close. They mark the card as one of the household continuity.

tool.note: There is no tool. The card is the legacy, not the working.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The legacy is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: A town or courtyard with an arch
landscape.note: The landscape is the town or courtyard, the place of the lineage. The arch is the passage between the generations.

architecture.note: The arch and the town are the architecture of the lineage. The arch marks the card as one of the passage between the generations.

threshold.note: The arch is the threshold between the old and the young, the past and the future. The card is the passage between them.

celestialBody.note: There is no celestial body. The legacy is ordinary, not cosmic.

weather.note: The weather is fair. The card is the calm day of the lineage.

symmetry.value: Balanced (the old man in the centre, the family around, the coins arranged)
symmetry.note: The composition is balanced. The card is the balance of the assembled lineage.

repetitionCount.note: The number ten is the number of completion. The ten coins mark the card as one of the completed legacy.

verticalAxis.value: The arch above, the family below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the arch to the family. The arch is the passage, the family is the gathered lineage.

horizontalAxis.value: The old man in the centre, the family around
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the lineage: the old man is in the centre, the family is around.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figures are upright.

clothing.value: Rich robes on the old man, varied dress on the family
clothing.note: The rich robes mark the old man as one of the wealth; the varied dress marks the family as distinct persons. The card is the gathered lineage.

nudity.note: The figures are clothed. Their legacy is mediated by their ordinary dress.

crown.note: There is no crown. The old man is not a ruler; he is the one who has accumulated.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of legacy, not of suffering.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figures are free.

water.note: There is no water. The card is a card of earth, not of water.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of earth, not of fire.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the town, not of the garden.

stone.note: Stone is present as the arch and the town, the architecture of the lineage.

polarity.note: The Ten of Pentacles' remedy-pair is the Ten of Swords: earth and air, legacy and ending. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Ten of Pentacles' legacy is the Ten of Swords' ending: sometimes the legacy needs to be corrected by the recognition of the ending that makes it possible.

prescribedAct.value: Name one thing today that you have inherited, and let it be the legacy.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of inheritance. The Ten of Pentacles' lesson is that the legacy is not the accumulation; it is the passing on.

detailedReading: The Ten of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of legacy. Its numerical degree is ten — the number of completion and the return to the beginning — and the figures are an old seated man, with a family group around him, ten coins arranged in the Tree of Life pattern, and an arch. The landscape is the town or courtyard, the place of the lineage. There is no written word, no wound, and no binding: the card is a card of human legacy, not of suffering, and not of restraint. The symmetry of the composition confirms that it is the balance of the assembled lineage. The prescribed act follows from this: name one thing today that you have inherited, and let it be the legacy. The remedy is ending — the Ten of Swords — because the legacy needs to be corrected by the recognition of the ending that makes it possible.
